English and AI

Deploy Your App with an AI Agent

To deploy an app means to publish it on the internet, so other people can open it with a link. When you ask an AI agent to deploy your app, the agent tells you to choose a few settings on the website. This guide shows those settings in order.

Your service
12345678

Before you start

You need these three things.

  • An app that already works on your local computer. Local means your own computer, not the internet.
  • A CloudflareVercel account. The free plan is enough.
  • Your API key for the AI model, if your app uses an AI model. If you do not have a key, ask your instructor. The instructor will give you an API key.

Steps in this guide

  1. Ask your agent to deploy
  2. Read what the agent needs
  3. Make the token
  4. Give the token to the agent
  5. Check your address
  6. The agent deploys your app
  7. Add your API key as a Secret
  8. Check the link
1

Ask your agent to deploy

Your app now runs only on your local computer. To publish it on the internet, send this prompt to your agent.

Your prompt

Deploy this app to Cloudflare.

2

Read what the agent needs

The agent cannot enter your Cloudflare account alone. It needs a token from you. A token is a permission. With it, the agent can upload your app to your account.

The agent might ask

I will deploy your app to Cloudflare. I need an API token from your account. Please make it with these settings.

  • Template: Edit Cloudflare Workers
  • Account: your account
  • Zone: All zones from an account, your account
  • More permissions: none

Please also check your subdomain.

This table shows where each setting is on the screen.

The agent might sayOn the Cloudflare screen
TemplateA card with the name Edit Cloudflare Workers
Account, or Account ResourcesThe box Account policy. Click the pencil icon.
Zone, or Zone ResourcesThe box Zone policy. Click the pencil icon.
One more permissionInside Account policy, the search field for permissions
Note
Your agent may use different words. The settings are the same. If your app uses a database, the agent can request one more permission. Add the permission that the agent names.
3

Make the token

Open dash.cloudflare.com and enter your account. Then follow the pictures. Each group is one line from the agent. Click a picture to see it bigger.

Open the token page

Template: Edit Cloudflare Workers

Zone: All zones from an account, your account

Account: your account

Check and create

Be careful
Cloudflare now shows the token. It appears only one time. Copy it before you close the page.
4

Give the token to the agent

  1. Make a new text file in your project folder. Name it cloudflare_token.txt.
  2. Paste the token into the file. Save the file.
  3. Send this prompt to tell the agent where the token is.
Your prompt

The Cloudflare token is in cloudflare_token.txt. Read the file. Do not show the token in the chat. Do not upload this file.

Be careful
Do not paste the token into the chat. Do not write the token in your code. A token is like a password.
5

Check your address

On Cloudflare, your link has three parts.

your-app-nameThe name of your app.your-subdomainOne name for your whole account.workers.devAlways the same.

Cloudflare gives your account a subdomain automatically. Usually it is made from your ID. You can see it here.

If this subdomain is fine for you, this step is complete. If you want a different subdomain, you have two choices.

Choice A: Change the name of this subdomain

The subdomain gets a new name. The old name stops working.

Be careful
If you change the name, the links of all your apps on this account change too.

Choice B: Keep this subdomain and create a new one

One account has only one subdomain. So a new subdomain needs a new account. The old subdomain and its apps stay the same.

Note
The token must be for the account that you deploy to. If you create a new account, make the token for the new account. In step 3, choose the new account in Zone policy and Account policy.
6

The agent deploys your app

Now the agent has all it needs. It uploads your app. This takes about one minute. Then it gives you the link.

The agent might say

The deployment is complete. Your app is here:

https://your-app-name.your-subdomain.workers.dev

You can also see the link on the Workers & Pages page, under the name of your app.

7

Add your API key as a Secret

Do this step if your app uses an AI model. The API key must stay on the server. You add it on the Cloudflare website, so the key never appears in the chat.

The agent might ask

Your app reads the key with the name OPENAI_API_KEY. Please add it as a Secret with exactly this name.

Note
In the picture, the box after Secret is still empty. You must click it before you save. After you save, the value shows as Value encrypted, and nobody can read it again. The button also deploys the app again, so the key works immediately.
8

Check the link

  1. Open the link in a private window, or on your phone.
  2. The page must open without a login page.
  3. Use the app one time. If your app uses an AI model, check that the AI answer appears.
  4. If all of this works, the deployment is complete. Submit this link.

After the deployment

  • You changed your app. Ask the agent: Deploy again. The link stays the same.
  • The project is finished. Open the token page again and delete the token.
1

Ask your agent to deploy

Your app now runs only on your local computer. To publish it on the internet, send this prompt to your agent. Include the word production.

Your prompt

Deploy this app to Vercel. Deploy to production.

Note
Vercel has two kinds of deployment. A production deployment is public. A preview deployment requires a Vercel login from other people. If you do not say production, the agent can choose preview.
2

Read what the agent needs

The agent cannot enter your Vercel account alone. It needs a token from you. A token is a permission. With it, the agent can upload your app to your account.

The agent might ask

I will deploy your app to Vercel. I need a token from your account. Please make it with these settings.

  • Token Name: any name
  • Scope: your projects
  • Expiration: 7 Days

This table shows where each setting is on the screen.

The agent might sayOn the Vercel screen
Account SettingsA small gear icon in the menu at the bottom left. The words Account Settings are not on the screen.
TokensThe last item in the left menu of the settings page
Scope: your projectsThe option with your account name and the word projects
3

Make the token

Open vercel.com and enter your account. Then follow the pictures. Click a picture to see it bigger.

For Expiration, choose 7 Days. After that time the token stops working, and that is safer. The list has these options: 1 Hour, 1 Day, 7 Days, 30 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days, 180 Days, 1 Year, No Expiration.

Be careful
Vercel now shows the token. It appears only one time. Copy it before you close the window.
4

Give the token to the agent

  1. Make a new text file in your project folder. Name it vercel_token.txt.
  2. Paste the token into the file. Save the file.
  3. Send this prompt to tell the agent where the token is.
Your prompt

The Vercel token is in vercel_token.txt. Read the file. Do not show the token in the chat. Do not upload this file.

Be careful
Do not paste the token into the chat. Do not write the token in your code. A token is like a password.
5

Check your address

On Vercel, your link has two parts.

your-app-nameThe name of your app.vercel.appAlways the same.
Note
If another person already uses the same name, Vercel can add extra letters to your link.
6

The agent deploys your app

Now the agent has all it needs. It uploads your app. This takes about one minute. Then it gives you the link.

The agent might say

The production deployment is complete. Your app is here:

https://your-app-name.vercel.app

Vercel shows two addresses for one app. To see them, open your project.

7

Add your API key as a Secret

Do this step if your app uses an AI model. The API key must stay on the server. You add it on the Vercel website, so the key never appears in the chat.

The agent might ask

Your app reads the key with the name OPENAI_API_KEY. Please add it as a Secret with exactly this name.

Note
Open your project first. The dashboard also has a menu item with the same name, but that one is for all projects.
Be careful
Vercel does not use the new key yet. The key works only after a new deployment. Send this prompt.
Your prompt

I added the API key. Deploy to production again.

8

Check the link

  1. Open the link in a private window, or on your phone.
  2. The page must open without a login page.
  3. Use the app one time. If your app uses an AI model, check that the AI answer appears.
  4. If all of this works, the deployment is complete. Submit this link.

After the deployment

  • You changed your app. Ask the agent: Deploy again. The link stays the same.
  • The project is finished. Open the token page again and delete the token.
The websites sometimes change their screens. These pictures are from November 2026. If a button is in a different place, find the same word on the screen.
